criteria.criterion: docs/decisions.md has a new decision with per-binary before and after times (lifecycle, job_plan, drain, retry, steward), measured the same way in the job and labeled measured, with the cause found for each and the total suite time.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. D126 has a table of before and after seconds for all five binaries, labeled measured, and the totals 649.4 s before and 389.3 s after. But it says: "The causes for the other four binaries are inferred from the same default flow and the per-binary times; they were not traced one by one." The cause for job_plan, drain, retry and steward is given as "the same", so a cause was found for lifecycle only. It also gives no measured total wall time for the full suite; the ~456 s figure is a sum built on the brain's compile time.

criteria.criterion: The decision records compile 67 s vs run 673 s (brain-measured, 4 cores). It lists cargo-nextest 0.9.148 (584 s vs 673 s, about 13%) as rejected. It lists sccache (D79) and a shared target dir as considered. It claims no unmeasured number.
criteria.evidence: Read from the diff. Case: "Brain-measured (4 cores): compile 67 s against run 673 s". Alternatives: nextest 0.9.148 rejected at 584 s vs 673 s, about 13%; sccache (D79) and a shared target directory considered, not adopted. The other numbers are labeled measured, or labeled as brain-reported and "not re-measured".

criteria.criterion: No test is deleted, ignored, filtered or has assertions weakened, and the test count is not lower than before. athena.toml, ci.yml and tool pins are unchanged. CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
criteria.evidence: The diff touches only CHANGELOG.md, checks.rs, secrets.rs and decisions.md. No test files changed, and it only adds tests: 2 in athena-core and 5 in athena-gate. athena.toml, ci.yml and tool pins are untouched. CHANGELOG.md has a new entry under ### Changed in the [Unreleased] section (line 8 heading).

criteria.criterion: Production changes are limited to the scan memo in crates/athena-gate/src/secrets.rs and the shorter poll schedule in crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs. Each leaves behavior unchanged and has a test: the memo equals uncached scanning, and the poll schedule still detects completion, failure and timeout.
criteria.evidence: secrets: 13 passed. These include the memo tests: results equal an uncached scan and a repeat is a hit; a moved ref is scanned again and the later token is found; inputs that do not resolve to ids are never kept; text equals an uncached scan; a different allow list gets its own entry. checks: 22 passed, including the_poll_schedule_doubles_to_a_cap_and_never_passes_the_deadline, the_poll_still_sees_completion_and_failure, and the existing a_check_past_its_deadline_is_killed. Only Ok results are cached, and ranges are keyed by resolved commit ids.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`. It passes with every test running, and the run is under 7 minutes on the job's machine. A failing test still fails the run.
criteria.evidence: The command is Athena's record, which I did not rerun: it passed with 1246 tests. The time goal is not met. D126 says: "the total is about 456 s, which is above the 7-minute (420 s) goal. The goal is not met by these changes alone." The producer's report also left this criterion unconfirmed. No evidence of a run under 420 s was given.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`. Both are clean.
criteria.evidence: Athena's records show both passed on this tree.

findings.summary: The stated goal, full cargo test under 7 minutes, is not met, and the change says so itself.
findings.evidence: "The run-time sum is 389.3 s. With the brain's compile time of 67 s ... the total is about 456 s, which is above the 7-minute (420 s) goal. The goal is not met by these changes alone."

findings.summary: The planned per-binary test changes were not made, so the remaining cost is left in place.
findings.evidence: These files are on the expected deliverables and planned files lists, but git diff --stat shows only 4 files changed. D126 says the 351 range scans left in lifecycle are most of what remains of its run time, and does not address them.

findings.summary: The cause is found for lifecycle only; for the other four binaries it is inferred, and the memo hit count is lifecycle-only.
findings.evidence: "The causes for the other four binaries are inferred ... they were not traced one by one." and "It was not counted for the other four binaries." Criterion 1 requires the cause found for each.

findings.summary: A process-wide memo with up to 4,096 entries of up to 64 KiB text in production, for a saving that mostly benefits tests.
findings.evidence: MEMO_MAX = 4096 and MEMO_TEXT_MAX = 64 KiB. D126 notes this tradeoff. The behavior is correct; it is a memory cost in long-running processes.

summary: The two production changes are sound and tested. The gitleaks scan memo in secrets.rs is keyed on the config text, the binary path and commit ids (or the scanned text), so a moved ref is scanned again. The shorter run_check poll schedule in checks.rs still sees completion, failure and timeout. I ran both new test sets and they pass; Athena's fmt, clippy and test records are clean. The change still fails the main goal. The request asked for a full `cargo test --locked` under 7 minutes. The new decision D126 says itself that the goal is not met: 389.3 s of test run time plus the brain's 67 s compile is about 456 s, above 420 s. The planned per-binary test changes (lifecycle, job_plan, drain, retry, steward, common/mod.rs, run.rs) were not made. D126 also says the causes for four of the five binaries were inferred, not traced, and the memo hit count was taken for lifecycle only.
